name: decomposed-source-modules
body:
apg's first-party source is well-decomposed, DRY, modular and maintainable: cohesive modules with a single clear responsibility, clear boundaries between them, and single-sourced shared logic. Line count is a signal that prompts an inspection, and a split is justified by improved cohesion.

Scope: repo-wide over first-party source, excluding vendored code (`src/cpplib/vendor/**`) and testdata (`testdata/**`) — the root Rust crate (`src/*.rs` + `build.rs`) and the eight frontend crates (`structlib`, `pylib`, `rustlib`, `cpplib` non-vendor sources, `javalib`, `golib`, `csharplib`, `tslib`).

DRY is a first-class part of this requirement: shared logic has exactly one definition. The scratch-repo test fixtures single-source in `rust.apg.testutil`, which defines the shared `rust.apg.testutil.with_cwd`, `rust.apg.testutil.wt_commit` and `rust.apg.testutil.wt_commit_paths` helpers once, for every module that uses them.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every first-party production module describes one concern; its name and contents agree.
- Shared logic has exactly one definition; a duplicated helper across modules is a defect.
- An over-large file receives a decomposition review, and any split is justified by improved cohesion.
- Completion is observable by review of the module set (names, responsibilities, and a duplicated-symbol inventory), independently of any line-count threshold.
